clips.send: Someone about to try their first multi-day fast sends this to the friend doing it with them, the practical anxiety of not knowing what to eat first, solved in one line.
clips.caption:
Before you start a multi-day fast, Kevin Trudeau says what you eat the three days leading up to it matters almost as much as the fast itself.

No meat, no protein. Just fruit, and ideally the soft kind: cantaloupe, honeydew, watermelon, papaya, mango. He skips berries before a fast because the seeds can be harder on the gut.

If you're having vegetables those three days, steam them soft. His reasoning: it eases your body into the transition instead of shocking it straight from a normal diet into nothing.

Most people who give up on a fast early, he says, skipped this step entirely.

Would you actually give yourself three days to prepare?

clips.send: A friend who just said they're starting a juice cleanse gets sent this - the awe that the whole thing runs on a strict 4-ounce rule most people doing it wrong have never heard of.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau's juice fast isn't just juice all day - it's measured down to the ounce.

Every meal is the same structure: 4 ounces of fresh juice mixed with 4 to 8 ounces of water, sipped slowly over 15 minutes so your body eases into the sugars instead of getting hit all at once.

Mornings rotate between cantaloupe, watermelon and honeydew, alone. Lunch mixes in apple, celery, kale and spinach. Dinner adds carrot for extra minerals. Nothing repeats two days in a row.

His point: a real fasting protocol isn't improvised, it's a system.

Would you actually measure your juice to the ounce?

#kevintrudeau #fasting #juicefast #healthtruth #naturalhealth #wbdaily

clips.send: Someone who just finished a juice fast forwards this to the friend about to break theirs with a burger, the anxious warning that rushing back to food undoes days of work.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau's juice fast protocol doesn't end the moment the fast does. Breaking it wrong, he says, can undo the benefit.

Day one after the fast: the same soft food as the pre-fast, pureed soup and fruit, nothing solid yet.

Day two: rice finally comes back. He recommends jasmine or white rice over brown, which he says is too rough on a system that just went without food.

Day three: real chewing returns, with raw or cooked vegetables, a salad, and fish.

His rule: no burger, no steak, straight off a fast. The body gets three days back in, the same way it got three days to prepare.

Would you have the patience for day one?
